explanation: Mixed: fires most on a zero digit inside a long run of zeros (e.g. '000000[0]'), and moderately on mid-word subword pieces of medical terms ('rheumat[oid]', 'med[ulla]'), plus assorted code tokens (import, os.path, __init__, localhost) and CJK byte fragments. Ordinary prose function words give only weak activation.

No clear shared feature. Top activations land on varied tokens: commas between function parameters in code, 'came' after 'I', digits inside copyright years ('20[1]2'), the space before a number in citations, Vietnamese 'thể', closing brackets in JSON. Strength is hard to predict from the token or its context.

Fires broadly on tokens that finish a short clause or phrase, often right before punctuation: discourse words like 'some', 'again', 'yes', 'now', 'all', 'Sometimes', and code tokens such as ');', '//', '.println'. The trigger is the position (the end of a phrase or start of a parallel phrase) more than the token's meaning. The pattern is diffuse.

Fires on the unit or size word that directly follows a number, or a number in a quantity expression: 'g' in '2 g/kg', 'million' after '$20', '-year' in '11-year-old', 'second', 'degrees', '-acre', 'V' in '220V', and a number after 'Round y to'. It also fires moderately on size adjectives in quantity contexts ('long', 'smaller', 'large', 'small').

Mixed. The strongest hits are the '8' in 'ISO-8859-1'. Other hits are 'mal' prefixes (malice, malonaldehyde, malady), digits inside model or ZIP codes, version '1.0' dots, medical word-piece fragments, and table or line separators. There is no single unifying context.

Fires on mid-word subword pieces of rare or foreign proper names and technical words, where the word is split into unusual fragments (Kanan[ask]is, Cioc[col]aterie, von [Str]ick, Russian 'ор'/'ик', He[isen]berg, Davy [Cro]ckett, radio[-ul]nar). It also fires on a few license-boilerplate tokens ('Copyright IN', 'CONDITIONS OF'). Common whole words fire weakly.

Fires on verbs and nouns of support, defense or protection directed at someone or something ('supporting', 'defend', 'side with', 'support', 'protect', 'protection', 'save'), and on the preposition or article right after a fight-or-support verb ('fight for the', 'coalition of'). There is a weaker spillover onto arithmetic tokens in 'Solve ...' equations.

Fires in news-style or report prose on time and recency words and dates that set up when something happened: 'Recent', 'recent', 'new report', 'fiscal year', year digits ('201[4]'), month or weekday names ('June', 'Oct', 'Tuesday'), and words like 'asked for' or 'seeking' comments. Triggers are mostly temporal framing near the start of a news sentence.

Fires on a word-ending or mid-word subword piece that completes a word split into fragments, often in foreign languages (Greek, Turkish, Portuguese) or rare words ('ammon[ium]', 'quadr[ature]', 'yaku[za]', 'APPEA[LED]'). It also fires on closing tokens in code such as ')', '</html', '++)'. Common whole English words fire weakly.

Fires on several kinds of tokens: license boilerplate ('subject to', 'the License', 'Apache Software License'), suffix pieces completing technical or biological words ('hepar[in]', 'congen[ital]', 'pup[ae]', 'hyosc[ine]'), digits inside hashes or HTML entities, and path pieces. There is no single concept.

Fires on the opening brace '{' with its newline, or on the first indentation, that starts the body of a class, function, method or namespace in code (C#, Java, PHP, JS, ObjC, C++, Python class body). Prose tokens give only weak activation.

Mixed. Hits include chemistry and biomedical word pieces ('C=C', 'germ-free', 'Porc[ine]', 'hist[ocom]patibility', 'substit[uted]'), 'District' in court names, code keywords ('nonatomic', 'const', '?:'), LaTeX pieces ('\to', 'f(R'), and '======' separators. No single context unites them.

Fires on paragraph-break whitespace or newline tokens at structural boundaries. Two common cases: the blank line or indentation after field declarations, just before a constructor or method in a Java-like class, and the '?

' or '.

' that ends a Q&A question before 'A:'. Plain newlines between ordinary prose paragraphs fire more weakly.

Fires on function words and numbers inside boilerplate or disclaimer and terms-of-service text: 'opinions expressed are', 'nor the names', 'or copy at', 'WITHOUT WARRANTIES', 'within 8-15 business days', 'more than 12 weeks'. It responds to the formulaic notice context more than to the specific token.
